title: Obsolete synchronous pagination delays the latest font reflow
symptom: An app-only trace of release artifact 3d05a… used a 50,407-character, chapter containing 1,200 numbered paragraphs plus one ending paragraph and the sequence 18-to-20-to-22-to-24-to-22 sp. Obsolete 20 sp pagination ran for 10,612.537 ms; the following 22 sp computation took 144.936 ms, while 24 sp was not computed. No screen recording or new app ANR overlapped the measurement.
root_cause: ChapterPageCalculations.pages holds its mutex while withContext(Dispatchers.Default) runs synchronous paragraph measurement, pagination and page-bottom fit checks. That synchronous path lacked cancellation checks. Cancelling the Job could discard the result only after the work returned, leaving the mutex occupied and the latest layout waiting behind obsolete work.
evidence: The final input command ended at trace-clock 3862.650 s. Obsolete computation ended at 3871.589136 s, and the new computation ended at 3871.735133 s.

This establishes approximately 8.939 s waiting for obsolete computation and 9.085 s from command completion to the new computation's end. These are computation timings, not measured final-presentation latency, percentile statistics or target-device performance.

In the final single sample, 20 sp took 171.979 ms, intermediate 22 sp 164.055 ms, 24 sp 175.235 ms and final 22 sp 2961.724 ms. The variation in the latest computation itself precludes a general speedup ratio or percentile claim. These timings end at computation completion, not measured screen presentation.
fix: Pass the current worker CoroutineContext into paragraph measurement and pagination, checking ensureActive at paragraph and page boundaries so obsolete work releases the mutex promptly.
Retain line measurement, source ranges and every page-bottom completeness check. Cancellation must terminate obsolete computation without weakening the completed result's text-integrity checks.

The new regression first failed because cancelled pagination returned normally instead of throwing CancellationException. After implementation, all seven ReaderPageLinePaginatorTest cases passed. The three real-rendering integrity cases and two reflow/pending-navigation cases also passed on the corresponding new device build in 92.045 seconds.

The same font sequence on final release 1e26f66378cae8776184bbde09e4dcf23957ba875869f07c62b280e06b142928 retained paragraph 0001 at actual 22 sp without an error or new ANR. After the last input command ended, the preceding 24 sp trace segment ended in 108.540 ms, final 22 sp work started in 119.871 ms and ended in 3081.595 ms. Trace end markers alone do not distinguish cancellation from normal completion; cancellation behavior is established separately by the regression and worker-context checks.
failed_attempts: Discarding stale results after synchronous pagination finishes protects state ordering but does not release computation capacity or the mutex early enough for the latest request.
impact: Obsolete pagination now checks the actual worker Job at paragraph and page boundaries, releasing the computation mutex when cancelled and never publishing partial pages. The covered input no longer waited seconds for the preceding computation after the final command. Individual native text-measure calls are not preempted, and this emulator evidence does not establish Xiaomi performance or universal latency thresholds.
